pr.title: Have init allow every project command except init, upgrade, and config changes
pr.head: 7f37082292c730e185a116b0a7cc962dbc6a58c3

summary: project init writes permission rules into your own Claude Code settings (~/.claude/settings.json) and your Codex rules (~/.codex/rules/projector.rules). Those rules decide which project commands an agent can run without a prompt or a refusal from the host's automatic approval, such as Claude Code's auto mode or Codex's approval reviewer. Until this change, init allowed only three commands: project review publish, project review hold, and project summary publish. Every other project command could stop for a prompt, which pushes agents toward editing Projector's files by hand or calling gh api directly.

This change allows every project command and asks only before the few that the author judges to reach outside Projector's own state. The two hosts get different shapes of rule, because their rule languages differ:

HostAllowedStill asks or falls through
Claude CodeBash(project *) in permissions.allowproject init, project upgrade, project config set and unset, project site with --prepare or --allow-prepare, project inbox answer, dismiss, and snooze, and any command line that starts with an option, such as project --root . init, through rules in permissions.ask
CodexNamed commands and subcommands, listed in CODEX_ALLOWinit, upgrade, config set and unset, create and edit, review gate, site build and serve, inbox answer, dismiss, and snooze, and any line that starts with an option. These match no rule and fall to Codex's usual approval, inside its sandbox.

init also removes the older, narrower allow rules it wrote before, and only from permissions.allow. site build and site serve refuse abbreviated options, so the ask rule for --prepare matches every spelling an agent can use. The documentation and three skills now describe the broad rule.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Allow rule: a host setting that runs a matching command with no prompt and, in Claude Code's auto mode, no classifier check.
  • Ask rule: a Claude Code setting that prompts for a matching command. Claude Code checks ask rules before allow rules, so an ask rule wins.
  • prefix_rule: a Codex rule that matches a command's first words exactly, with no wildcard.
  • Superseded rules: the narrow allow rules, such as Bash(project review publish *), that Bash(project *) now covers.

cards.html:

groups.title: The rules init writes
groups.kicker: What each host now allows, asks for, and drops
intro: src/projector/permissions.py holds the rules as constants and the two functions that write them. ALLOW is the one Claude Code allow rule, ASK the nine Claude Code ask rules, and SUPERSEDED the narrow rules that init removes. CODEX_ALLOW pairs each Codex pattern with the justification Codex shows, and builds the Codex file, which init rewrites whole.

Bash(project -*) exists because the CLI accepts --root and --projects-dir before the command name. Without it, project --root . init would match the allow rule and none of the command ask rules. Codex has no wildcard to express the same thing, so the Codex side lists the commands it allows. It leaves out every command that can run another program, because Codex runs an allowed command outside its sandbox.

tests/test_permissions.py pins one table of command lines to the decision each host reaches, including leading variable assignments such as VISUAL=…. A test fails when the parser gains a command or subcommand that the Codex rules neither allow nor leave out on purpose, and another checks that site build and serve refuse abbreviated prepare flags.

checks.text: The question to hold while reading: does every command the broad rule now allows stay inside Projector's own state? The excluded set is init, upgrade, config set and unset, the prepare flags of site build and serve, and inbox answer, dismiss, and snooze, which record the person's choice on an inbox item.

files.note: The rule constants, the module docstring that explains each choice, the Claude settings rewrite that adds ASK and drops SUPERSEDED, and the Codex rules.

checks.text: ASK covers project inbox answer, dismiss, and snooze, so an agent can no longer answer its own question unprompted. The review checked at this head that project inbox ans 1.a and project inbox --session s1 answer 1.a exit 2, so no other spelling reaches answer. The band runs these commands from its own process, so the person is never asked.

Superseded rules leave only permissions.allow. The review ran init against a scratch HOME: the narrow allow rules were replaced by Bash(project *), deny and existing ask entries stayed, and all nine ask rules were added.

files.note: The decision table for both hosts, and the test that ties the Codex list to the parser.

checks.text: site build and serve without a prepare flag stay allowed in Claude Code. They then run only a site.prepare command the person already allowed for that checkout.

groups.title: init and review rules
groups.kicker: The CLI's callers of the rules and their messages
intro: project init and project review rules call allow_commands, the renamed allow_publish. review rules only reports, so a review loop can learn before its first publish that the rules are missing. The messages now describe Projector's commands in general instead of naming three. The parser now builds site build and site serve with allow_abbrev=False, so --prep no longer parses as --prepare.
tests/test_projector.py replaces the three-rule expectations with a granted() helper and adds tests for the superseded rules and for ask rules added beside an existing allow rule.

files.note: The rename to allow_commands, reworded help and refusal messages, and allow_abbrev=False on site build and site serve.

checks.text: The review ran site build with --prep, --pre, and --prepar, and site serve with --allow-prep, at this head with Python 3.12. Each exited with unrecognized arguments, and none ran its command.

files.note: Settings fixtures move to granted(); new tests cover removal of superseded rules and the report-only path.

intro: docs/cli.md lists the ask rules, explains why Bash(project -*) exists, and shows the Codex file. The README and the fix-pr, review-pr, and start-review-loop skills now refer to Bash(project *) instead of the narrow rules.
